name: Agents Interacting with the Physical World
gist: Papers about agents that see and act in the real world or realistic simulations — like robots, autonomous driving, or interacting with computers.
explain: Some agents don't just process text or numbers; they perceive and act in the real world. A robot sees its environment through a camera, reasons about what it sees, and moves its arms to manipulate objects. An autonomous car sees traffic, pedestrians, and road markings, and decides how to steer and accelerate. These are tool-use problems too: the camera is a tool that gives perception, the motor is a tool that produces motion, and the agent has to chain them together. These papers cover how agents learn to perceive, reason, and act in scenarios where the physics is real and mistakes have real consequences.

The difficulty jumps dramatically here. In a text-based problem, if an agent guesses wrong, you reload and try again in milliseconds. In the real world or realistic simulation, a mistake might damage equipment, or the situation might have changed too much to recover from. The agent perceives the world at one moment, makes a decision, acts, and by the time it perceives again, the world might have evolved in unexpected ways. Perception is also noisy and ambiguous — maybe the agent isn't sure if that object is a cup or a can. And there are delays between decision and action that have to be accounted for. The agent can't just trial-and-error its way to success; it has to reason and be more careful.

Papers here focus on embodied agents — agents that learn by interacting with simulations or real environments. Some train agents on videos or simulations where mistakes are cheap, then transfer that knowledge to reality. Others focus on robotics, teaching robots to recognize objects, plan grasps, and manipulate them. Some papers tackle autonomous driving or agents that interact with computer interfaces like navigating a website to buy something. The underlying goal is agents that don't just think but act, and that can bridge the gap between understanding a situation and successfully manipulating the world to achieve a goal.

papers.title: Code2Video: A Code-centric Paradigm for Educational Video Creation
papers.contribution: Improves performance 40% over direct code generation and produces videos comparable to human-crafted tutorials, with TeachQuiz metric measuring knowledge recovery.

papers.title: Gecko: A Simulation Environment with Stateful Feedback for Refining Agent Tool Calls
papers.contribution: Consistently improves performance of various LLMs including GPT-4o, GPT-5, and Gemini-3.0-pro on BFCLv3 and tau^2-bench through simulation-based tool call refinement before real execution.

papers.title: LangForce: Bayesian Decomposition of Vision Language Action Models via Latent Action Queries
papers.contribution: Achieve 11.3% improvement on challenging OOD SimplerEnv benchmark, validating robust language grounding in robotic manipulation.

papers.title: ProPerSim: Developing Proactive and Personalized AI Assistants through User-Assistant Simulation
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that assistants adapted through user feedback steadily improve satisfaction across 32 diverse personas, uniting proactivity and personalization.

papers.title: Scaling Synthetic Task Generation for Agents via Exploration
papers.contribution: Generates 20k Android and 10k Ubuntu tasks enabling large-scale training of UI agents that improve success rates by up to 20.0% on mobile and 10.9% on computer-use scenarios without human annotation.

papers.title: Test-Time Adaptation for LLM Agents via Environment Interaction
papers.contribution: Both strategies demonstrate effectiveness across diverse agentic benchmarks with minimal computational cost, with dynamics grounding being particularly effective in complex environments.

papers.title: Turning Adaptation into Assets: Cross-Domain Bridging for Online Vision-Language Navigation
papers.contribution: IDEA enables training-free adaptation via asset sharing and achieves consistent superiority over existing TTA methods on REVERIE, R2R, and R2R-CE benchmarks.

papers.title: Zephyrus: An Agentic Framework for Weather Science
papers.contribution: Zephyrus outperforms text-only baselines by up to 35 percentage points on ZephyrusBench which includes tasks from basic lookups to advanced forecasting.

papers.title: AutoRPA: Efficient GUI Automation through LLM-Driven Code Synthesis from Interactions
papers.contribution: RPA functions generated by AutoRPA solve similar tasks while reducing token usage by 82-96%, significantly improving runtime efficiency and reusability.

papers.title: AutoWebWorld: Synthesizing Infinite Verifiable Web Environments via Finite State Machines
papers.contribution: Generates over 11,663 verified trajectories from 29 environments at $0.04 per trajectory, with 7B agent achieving state-of-the-art on WebVoyager, showing clear scaling law with synthetic data volume.

papers.title: Beyond Static Endpoints: Tool Programs as an Interface for Flexible Agentic Web Services
papers.contribution: Reduces end-to-end latency by up to 53.4% and client-side traffic by up to 96.1%, with larger gains under higher network latency.

papers.title: CAPTCHA Solving for Native GUI Agents: Automated Reasoning-Action Data Generation and Self-Corrective Training
papers.contribution: ReCAP substantially improves CAPTCHA-solving success over base agents while maintaining strong performance on general GUI-agent benchmarks.

papers.title: DocOS: Towards Proactive Document-Guided Actions in GUI Agents
papers.contribution: Reveals dual bottlenecks: agents struggle to locate relevant information during proactive search and fail to ground retrieved instructions into precise GUI actions in interactive environments.

papers.title: Embodied Task Planning via Graph-Informed Action Generation with Large Language Models
papers.contribution: GiG achieves Pass@1 gains of up to 22% on Robotouille Synchronous, 37% on Asynchronous, and 15% on ALFWorld while maintaining comparable or lower computational cost.

papers.title: Estimating the Empowerment of Language Model Agents
papers.contribution: Empowerment strongly correlates with task performance and serves as goal-agnostic metric complementing task-success measures for LM-agent evaluation.

papers.title: Go-Browse: Training Web Agents with Structured Exploration
papers.contribution: Fine-tuning a 7B parameter language model on this dataset achieves 21.7% success rate on WebArena benchmark, beating GPT-4o mini by 2.4% and exceeding state-of-the-art for sub-10B models by 2.9%.

papers.title: HAMLET: Hyperadaptive Agent-based Modeling for Live Embodied Theatrics
papers.contribution: Creates expressive, coherent theatrical experiences with independent actor decision-making and scene state changes.

papers.title: Implicit Intelligence - Evaluating Agents on What Users Don’t Say
papers.contribution: Evaluate 16 frontier models on implicit reasoning; best model achieves only 48.3% pass rate, revealing large gap between literal instruction-following and contextual reasoning.

papers.title: Neural Synchrony Between Socially Interacting Language Models
papers.contribution: Neural synchrony between LLMs is strongly correlated with their social performance, demonstrating parallels in internal dynamics between human and LLM social interaction.

papers.title: OmniActor: A Generalist GUI and Embodied Agent for 2D&3D Worlds
papers.contribution: OmniActor outperforms agents trained solely on GUI or embodied data in their respective tasks, particularly excelling at GUI tasks with the unified framework.

papers.title: PRISM: Perception Reasoning Interleaved for Sequential Decision Making.
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art image-based models on ALFWorld and R2R benchmarks with automatic goal-oriented perception pipeline and no handcrafted questions.

papers.title: QLCoder: A Query Synthesizer For Static Analysis of Security Vulnerabilities
papers.contribution: QLCoder reliably generates executable, up-to-date CodeQL queries through contextual engineering, iterative feedback, and structured tool interaction.

papers.title: Query-Aware Flow Diffusion for Graph-Based RAG with Retrieval Guarantees
papers.contribution: QAFD-RAG provides first statistical guarantees for query-aware graph retrieval and shows consistent improvements over state-of-the-art graph-based RAG methods.

papers.title: Vision2Web: A Hierarchical Benchmark for Visual Website Development with Agent Verification
papers.contribution: A 193-task benchmark from real-world websites with 918 prototype images and 1,255 test cases, revealing substantial performance gaps in state-of-the-art models on full-stack tasks.

papers.title: Weasel: Out-of-Domain Generalization for Web Agents via Importance-Diversity Data Selection
papers.contribution: Weasel improves out-of-domain performance with roughly 9.7-12.5x training speedups over standard fine-tuning across WebArena, WorkArena, and MiniWob benchmarks.

papers.title: WebWorld: A Large-Scale World Model for Web Agent Training
papers.contribution: WebWorld achieves simulation performance comparable to Gemini-3-Pro; Qwen3-14B trained on WebWorld-synthesized trajectories improves +9.2% on WebArena reaching GPT-4o performance levels.

papers.title: Whom to Query for What: Adaptive Group Elicitation via Multi-Turn LLM Interactions
papers.contribution: Achieves 12% relative improvement on CES at 10% respondent budget for population-level response prediction.
